verdict.line: You lose if Garen lands Q's silence into a level 6+ all-in while you're already under half HP; you win almost every trade once E is up and his Q is down.

brief.thesis: Darius's E (Apprehend) is the one tool in this matchup Garen has no answer for — it drags him back into range and removes his ability to disengage from a fight he's losing, while Darius's passive (Hemorrhage) stacking wins any extended trade Garen agrees to. Garen's only real counters are landing Q's silence before Darius starts his combo, and burying him with R (Demacian Justice) once level 6 hits. Outside of those two windows, Darius simply out-trades him.

If you're below ~60% HP and he has Q and R both available, disengage instead of trading — you cannot out-silence a silence.

yourWindow.what: The moment you have E, look to pull Garen mid-wave while his Q is on cooldown — without the silence he has no way to interrupt your E into W into auto into Q sequence, and your passive stacks snowball the trade decisively in your favor.

brief.thesis: K'Sante is a resistance-stacking tank whose passive proc scales off his own bonus armor and magic resist, so flat AP does very little into him — you beat him with percent-max-health magic damage and magic penetration, never with burst. The flip side is that your R (Realm of Death) steals a percentage of his stats, so ulting him doesn't just remove the enemy frontline for seven seconds, it lets you wear his tankiness while you do it. That stat theft, not the lane, is the real win condition in this matchup.

brief.thesis: Olaf's E (Reckless Swing) is true damage to both of you, so stacking armor doesn't make trading into him free the way it does against most top laners. Worse, his R (Ragnarok) grants immunity to all disables, which directly no-sells the two abilities your whole kit is built around — E (Facebreaker)'s stun and R (The Show Stopper)'s suppression grab simply fail to lock him down while it's active. This matchup is decided by whether you fight on your cooldown timers or his.
